OwnerName: Lindsay Park Bloodstock, R & C Legh Racing Pty Ltd Et Al
Spotlight: Resuming (21-weeks). Recent 1st at a jump-out here. Classy conveyance. Generally comes to hand quickly. Looks hard to beat with Blake Shinn on board.

OwnerName: Ms J McAlpine, Philippa Duncan Bloodstock Et Al
Spotlight: First-up (18-weeks). Last prep was highlighted by a G1 placing. Proven fresh performer. Has form this track and distance and a nice weight drop. Worth a look.

OwnerName: J P M Ma, A K Y Leung & Mrs J R McGrath
Spotlight: Resuming (39-weeks). Very speedy type. Nabbed on the wire in Open company first-up last campaign while warmed up with a synthetic trial & winning a recent Cranbourne jump-out. Watch closely.

OwnerName: Seymour Bloodstock, B W James Et Al
Spotlight: Freshened. Not disgraced in soft going at Sunshine Coast. Switching to 1200m. Can challenge.

OwnerName: Lindsay Park Bloodstock Pty Ltd, P B Devitt Et Al
Spotlight: Turned on the speed and fended off challengers to narrowly prevail this course 4 Jul. Unbeaten at track and distance. Well placed for a repeat performance.

OwnerName: Wessel Thoroughbreds, R H Morrison Et Al
Spotlight: Let-up (42-days). Performance just fair in the Eye Liner at Ipswich when went around $10. Since trialled at Caulfield Heath 16 Jul. Each way claims.
Great run at Swan Hill 5 Jun. Made the running but soon off the bit and weakened noticeably this course last time. Drops back in trip now. Could run into the exotics.
Just missed in a crackerjack finish in the (Bm88) at Flemington over this trip. Can play a role.

OwnerName: Mailbag Windstorm, C C F C Group Et Al
Spotlight: Now 5 weeks between runs. Well back and never sighted at Caulfield at first run for new trainer at long odds. Usually gets back. Keener on others here.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Useful on her day; highly tried and not at best so far this year, but she ran respectably when never-nearer fourth of eight in Irish Group 3 (1m2f, good to firm) two weeks ago; moves into unknown territory trip-wise but her pedigree gives hope that she'll stay and this is a drop in grade.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Listed winner and Group 3 runner-up for the Gosdens last year; has shown she retains all her ability, fourth in Group 2 over C&D (good to firm; wore tongue-strap) last month; this is easier and she should be thereabouts in a first-time hood.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Reliable type whose wins have come in 1m2f and 1m6f handicaps; good fourth on her only attempts at Listed company but she'll need a personal best if she's to make a winning reappearance after ten months off.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Best effort when winning Goodwood handicap (1m4f, good) in May; respectable third in C&D Listed race two weeks ago, racing freely and finding no extra; may not have reached her ceiling just yet and she's high on the list.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: From a family that has served these connections well; 0-10 since her debut success but she finished close behind Orionis when fifth in C&D Listed race (7-4 favourite) last time; previous two efforts read even better and she's a major player with a visor replacing cheekpieces.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Has improved with each run this year, winning maiden at Ripon (1m3f, good) and handicap at Salisbury (1m4f, good to firm; dug deep to see off main challenger by a neck), both in small fields; this is a sterner assignment but she's still unexposed and in good hands.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won her first two races; disappointing when favourite for Lingfield Oaks Trial in the spring but firmly back on track when second in French Listed event (1m4f, good; collared late on after being clear over 1f out) six weeks ago; still has untapped potential.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies & Mares) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Sea The Stars half-sister to the same connections' Oaks winner Soul Sister; arrives on an upward curve after easy novice win at Lingfield and unlucky second in handicap at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm; stayed on well after being short of room); plenty to find on bare form in this higher grade but she should be well suited by this step up in trip and cannot be discounted.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Unique Retreats, P Morrall & J Blackburn
Spotlight: Cost 160,000euros at the breeze-ups in May; justified favouritism with a front-running success at Beverley (5f, good to firm; Battle Fever second) four weeks ago; more to come and he's the one to beat.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Down the field in two 5f runs last month; minor nurseries beckon.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Never in the hunt in a 5f novice at Newcastle five weeks ago (18-1); should do much better at some point.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Never looked like getting to Palm Reader when second at Beverley (5f, good to firm) four weeks ago; no improvement for stepping up to 6f at Hamilton two weeks ago; 7lb turnaround in the weights may be insufficient to turn the tables.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 92,000gns yearling; second foal; half-brother to 7f AW winner Espona Bay (RPR 71); dam 5f 2yo winner (89), half-sister to 7f winners Bendy Spirit and The Toff; stable operating at a healthy strike-rate with 2yos this season; betting useful.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Modest form in two 5f maidens 98 days apart (gelded after debut); improvement essential.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd
Spotlight: 33-1 and always in rear on his debut at Beverley (5f, good to firm) 12 days ago; best watched.

RaceName: John & Paula 25th Wedding Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 150-1 when finishing down the field on last week's Newcastle debut (6f, AW); needs a big step forward.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: The future looked bright when he won the Melrose at York (1m6f, good to firm) last August but he's not built on that significantly; well held back in Britain for two Group races this May when last seen; off 12lb higher than in the Melrose, this return to a handicap may also be tough.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won this race in 2024 before embarking on a long losing run; he's broken that with two 2m wins on the AW this year, most notably in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle last time; second in valuable race at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) in May was followed by a blip here; back up another 4lb since Newcastle but not entirely ruled out.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2023 Royal Ascot winner who has also tasted the high life in top hurdle races; his attentions have been turned back to the Flat this year and he hasn't been in peak form; falling in the weights but still needs a revival; good 5lb claimer is enlisted.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 0-6 in handicaps, with regular progress/promise but not when favourite last time at Royal Ascot where he raced freely early on and ran out of steam after challenging over 2f out (finished 8l sixth of 17); it's much too early to forget his reappearance promise (also 1m4f on good to firm) but that latest run also casts some doubt on the suitability of this new trip.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Not a prolific winner, with his waiting tactics, but he was fourth in the Ebor at York (1m6f, good to firm) last August off a 2lb higher mark; ran creditably on reappearance, before neither start since panned out favourably; only ninth in this last year on his only run at Goodwood.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2-5 in France and also scored in December in Bahrain for new connections; fourth of eight at Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago was probably his best form but better is needed and he didn't settle well enough behind horses that day, so is seemingly not crying out for this longer trip.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Close third in this last year and a creditable, running-on fourth of 16 at Royal Ascot (1m6f, good to firm) latest start; strong each-way chance.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Contested three Group races last summer; it's been 1m4f handicaps (good to firm) this season, registering his highest rating when fourth of eight at Newmarket in May but two disappointing shows at Ascot have followed; blinkered latest; stays at least 1m5f (unraced over this far) and he's 6lb lower than at Newmarket, but some caution is advised at present.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Upset in the stalls when a disappointing favourite at this meeting last year (subsequently gelded); had a 1m6f win next time and solid performances when beaten about 3l on all three starts this season, sixth of 16 when back up to 1m6f at Royal Ascot latest; others saw it out better that day but he should have serious each-way claims.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Stepped up to 1m6f with cheekpieces enlisted for last two starts and won them both, doing it smoothly at this track (good) and having to battle when prevailing by a neck in valuable race at Newmarket (good to firm); raised another 3lb but looks a serious contender once again.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: J William Rowley & S P C Woods
Spotlight: Won five-runner race here (upped to 2m, good) in May and made most when fifth of 20 in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle (2m, AW); no room over 1f out at Newbury two weeks ago but the speed with which he dropped out when jockey gave up was still rather disconcerting; place chance if bouncing back.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 1m4f festival wins off much lower marks at Chester and Epsom last July when trained by the Moores; returned to Flat with an eye-catching effort at Royal Ascot (2m4f, good to firm; 12-1) last month, turning for home towards rear but running on into sixth of 20; back down in trip but one to note.

RaceName: Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Two big runs over 1m4f here, including when third of nine in Listed race in May; not quite so good in two Ascot handicaps (1m6f/1m4f) since and there's a bit more to prove at this trip but that Listed run reads well.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Slightly disappointing when dropped to 5f for latest run and remains unproven on ground quicker than good, but was placed twice over 6f beforehand (maiden/handicap) and can play a major role if aided by first-time blinkers.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Bettered low-key debut when second at Newcastle (7f, AW) in December, despite racing too freely; makes turf debut after 225-day break but the drop in trip could be a good move; big player if fully tuned up.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Boasts the best form in this line-up, having twice finished second (once over C&D) on fast ground in the spring, but seems to have lost his way since; beaten over 18l when last of four at Ripon (6f, good) a fortnight ago and arrives here with questions to answer.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beaten about 7l when fourth of six in run-of-the-mill Redcar maiden (7f, good to firm) on debut a fortnight ago; needs improvement here but is entitled to have learnt from that outing.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well beaten on both outings, the latest here (7f, good) on seasonal/stable debut in June; drops back to 6f with hood added today.

RaceName: Aalberts IPS Pegler Valves Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Out of a Japanese 6f/7f dirt winner; soundly beaten when last of three on recent debut at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm); now tries sprinting.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Six-time Flat winner was beaten 14l off 97 in a Ballinrobe handicap hurdle last time so can't be fancied on that form.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Group 3 winner in France and was second in a German Group 1 last year; sold for 400,000euros since; not a bad hurdling debut at Killarney but was poor back on the Flat at Royal Ascot; however, has a solid shout back hurdling and looks the stable first-string.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Five Flat wins in UK for Sir Mark Prescott up to 2m1f and rated 87; bought for 19,000gns last year; a concern that he has been off the track since but is worth a market check.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: French bumper winner was second in a Grade 3 in that sphere when last seen in April 2025; a concern that he has been off for so long but still has to be respected from this yard even though he looks the second-string.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Runner-up on second point start; showed a glimpse of ability in a Tramore bumper but needs to do much better here.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Second runner for yard; beaten 12l in a Roscommon handicap hurdle last time and can't be fancied here on that form.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Four Flat wins and is rated 89 in that sphere; was never involved in the Connacht Hotel handicap here five days ago; best hurdle run when second at Killarney last time, a mistake at the last costing him; should be in the mix.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a Fairyhouse bumper on debut for Mags Mullins last November, beating the smart Moonverrin into second; has since changed hands and looks to have been targetted at this meeting so has to be feared; the market can be a guide.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Smart Flat sort has won twice and seems to stay 1m2f; a solid run in a Curragh Group 3 in April and now rated 101; has stamina to prove on hurdling debut but could be a player if jumping soundly.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Soundly beaten in all starts in different disciplines so is one for handicaps in time.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Two wins up to 1m4f when trained by William Haggas before being sold for 30,000gns; makes hurdling debut after an absence and could run well; the market can help.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: A 1m2f AW winner for Jane Chapple Hyam last year; beaten 29l in a Cork maiden hurdle on stable debut last month; needs plenty of improvement from that; tongue-tie on.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Soundly beaten in a bumper and maiden hurdle at Bellewstown so is best watched for the time being.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Beaten a long way in three maiden hurdles on soft ground in the spring; however, has respected connections and is likely to do better on this sounder surface.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Beaten a long way in a Punchestown maiden hurdle on debut for Tony Mullins; passed over today.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Best point run came when second in February; well beaten in a Downpatrick maiden hurdle; lots to find; hood on.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Was weakening when fell two out on sole point start; tongue-tie on for rules debut; best watched.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Respectable midfield finishes in both maiden hurdle runs and looks one for handicaps in time.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Placed in a point; won a Naas bumper in testing ground before third in a Grade 2 bumper at Leopardstown; not as good in an Aintree Grade 2 since on better ground; should be capable of running well on hurdle bow.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Beaten a long way at Kilbeggan on debut and passed over today.

Formerly a miler but has gained last three wins over 1m2f, the most recent in Bahrain; well held in major handicap returned to home soil last time; bit to prove off current mark back down in trip; Lexie Clarkson claims 7lb but has limited experience.

Nosed ahead in the final strides at York (7f) last time, ending a two-year losing spell and showing he retains plenty of ability aged eight; back up just 2lb he remains well treated on historical data; won the Thirsk Hunt Cup over C&D in 2023; should remain competitive.

Record of 3-11 in France for Henri-Francois Devin, most recently prevailing narrowly in big-field handicap at Longchamp in May; sold for 80,000euros since; likely faces a stiffer task off opening British mark but market support should be heeded.
Formerly smart but is currently out of sorts, as several duck eggs next to his name reflect, and hasn't scored on turf for nearly three years (gained last two wins on Newcastle AW); opposed.

Commenced career with two wins, including Listed; 0-6 and patchy form-wise since but proved resurgent in York handicap (1m; debut for new stable) most recently and is interesting off current mark assuming he builds on that effort.

Useful on his day and has a record of 2-3 over C&D, notably a success off current mark in this year's Thirsk Hunt Cup; not particularly solid on form elsewhere since but the return to this scenario may have a positive effect; not dismissed.

Scored twice in 2024 and three times in 2025; gradually back to form this season, creditable second in useful handicap at York (1m) most recently; appears to be on his way to regaining the winning thread and looks a must for the shortlist.

Generally in good form, mostly on AW, for current stable and latest effort is best forgiven (race didn't pan out favourably); not disgraced in most recent turf attempt but is still seeking a first success in this sphere and is somewhat hostage to fortune the way he races.

Campaigned mostly at the Newmarket tracks this term, winning in May and respectable third last time; has shown versatility in the past but looks weighted to the hilt off current mark and this step back up in class adds to the difficulty.

Front-running tactics backfired at the Newmarket July festival last time when bidding for a 1m hat-trick after Class 4 wins at Carlisle; remains on career-high mark and is upped further in grade, so needs to resume his improvement.

Sole 3yo in this field; maiden last term; gelded prior to posting form figures of 131 (over 7f-1m) this season, the wins on sharp, left-handed tracks, namely Catterick (good) and Chester (good to soft); open to further improvement, should take well to Thirsk and receives weight all round; respected.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Down the field in the Group 2 Queen Mary at Royal Ascot, but she'd previously come from the rear to win the Listed Marygate at York (5f, good); should be just as effective over 6f and may still have untapped potential.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Highly tried since debut win at Bath (5.7f, firm) in May; seemed to show improvement when sixth of eight in C&D Group 2 three weeks ago, although 50-1 and no threat; that run hasn't been missed by the handicapper.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Improving with each run and won going away from two rivals in nursery at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) 11 days ago; raised 5lb but should be well suited by this return to 6f and may well complete a hat-trick.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Green on debut but hasn't looked back since and she forced a dead-heat in C&D Listed race (good to firm; 100-30) last time; may have more in the tank and she's high on the list once more.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Could finish only in midfield in the Super Sprint at Newbury (4-1) last month but she was done no favours by the draw; better judged on a clearcut maiden win at Goodwood (6f, soft) the time before; remains open to improvement and may well get back on track here.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Has taken off for front-running tactics and cheekpieces on her last two starts, winning nurseries at Catterick and Thirsk (both 6f, good to firm); up 11lb in total but keeps improving and should make another bold bid.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Got up late on to win maiden at Chester (5.5f, good) in May but ran poorly when upped to 7f for nursery there two months later; perhaps this intermediate trip will suit but she's on a retrieval mission.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Gained deserved win after three second places in maiden at Lingfield (6f, good to firm) 17 days ago, no more than workmanlike in landing the odds; in deeper here and 3lb out of weights but she may not be fully exposed.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Like Rollthedicebaby, she finished in mid-division in the Super Sprint (80-1) last time, but she had no excuses on account of the draw; up against it here from 4lb out of the handicap.

9yo who has won the last two runnings of this race (good to firm/good to soft) and has run well on both starts this season, most recently posting a cosy Listed win at Beverley (1m4f, good to firm); leading claims.

OwnerName: T & Mrs L Standish & Mrs A Spence
Spotlight: He's run well on both visits to Goodwood, latest a close third in 1m2f Listed race here (good) in May after an absence, and the late headway he made when eighth in the Listed Wolferton at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) suggests this step up in trip could be a good move; each-way chance.

He was returning from a year off when down the field in the Wolferton at Royal Ascot in June, and may have needed that first run for Kevin Philippart De Foy; classy performer for Clive Cox prior to £2,000,000 sale, making the frame in several Group 1s, and can have a big say if back to his best.

Won Meydan handicap (9.5f, good) in March and ran well in defeat in Listed races on next two starts (including here over 1m2f); however, no match for Al Aasy in Listed race at Beverley (1m4f, good to firm) four weeks ago and others have more substance to their claims.

Late headway once in the clear in the Listed Wolferton Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) in June, finishing seventh of 16, and outclassed in the Eclipse since (well beaten at 100-1); drops back in grade and the step back up in trip is worth a go, but he's 0-13 in Group/Listed races since winning the London Gold Cup in May 2024 and may again find a few too good.

Ex-French 4yo who won Group 3 at Saint-Cloud (10.5f, good) last May; respectable Listed efforts on last two starts (including C&D) but hasn't shown enough on those outings to suggest he'll be making an impact today.

Lightly raced 4yo who won at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm) in May on his second start since being gelded and followed up in the Duke Of Edinburgh Handicap at Royal Ascot (1m4f, good to firm); he's by Frankel out of a Group 1 winner and could take this rise in grade in his stride; key player.

Didn't really take to hurdling but she relished the step up in trip in this code when easily winning a 13-runner handicap at the Curragh (1m4f, good) in June; she has to prove that brilliance was no one-off but it was certainly an impressive performance and she could have a part to play today.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: All three races were over 7f on good ground, best on second occasion when third of seven at Sandown despite having traffic issues and stumbling; raced up with pace, but faded, when favourite there last time; goes handicapping and his earlier promise can't be forgotten.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Third at Beverley (7.4f, good) and justified favouritism in a five-runner novice at Ayr (7f, good to firm) four weeks later, outpaced over 2f out but rallying strongly; the fourth from that Ayr race is the only one to have run since and he won; while 1m might have made more appeal, this one clearly looks capable of better.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Favourite both starts, when unable to hold off a strong finisher at Leicester (7f, good) and unable to threaten at Chester (6f, good; third at 11-10); the winner on first occasion took the Group 2 Vintage at Goodwood this week for his second win since, and the third also won next time; moving back up to 7f should help this one on nursery debut.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: Spg Property, Alfa Site & Graeme Curnow
Spotlight: Second at Wolverhampton (6f, AW; 66-1) in June, always front rank, was much better than his runs on good ground either side; just behind Eighth Immortal at Chester (6f) latest, with that rival going past him; late foal who's bred to stay 1m+.

RaceName: Bapp Group Of Companies Bapp Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Modest form on first two starts (6f, AW/good) and stiff task when well beaten on soft ground for latest; gelded since; bred to stay 1m/1m2f in time and needs a market check on this handicap debut.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual hurdle winner and was third in this race in 2023 off 6lb higher; regressive over fences last season but a decent Flat run at Killarney last time; could run well.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has been in the form of her life at present, winning handicaps at Ballinrobe (2m) and Kilbeggan (2m4f); got a 10lb rise for that and back down in trip but still has to be on the shortlist.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual-purpose winner was well beaten at Punchestown on his last hurdle run but ran a decent race on the Flat at Tramore since; needs to find more.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual-purpose winner won his last hurdle race over C&D last October; ran a solid race from the front to be third to Putapoundinthejar at Bellewstown last time; 3lb better off and cheekpieces added; chance.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Four of his five wins came in Britain, with three at Cartmel; posted a solid run at Ballinrobe last time and should run well again off 1lb higher.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual-purpose winner is at his best on testing ground; last win came on the Flat here in October 2025; well beaten on the level here three days ago.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual-purpose winner won a Listowel handicap hurdle in June but was beaten 13l by Putapoundinthejar at Bellewstown last time; has to rebound.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Killarney novice hurdle winner last October has run well at times in defeat since, notably back at that track in May; poor behind Spy at Listowel since so questions.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Seamus Perry & Brian P Larkin & Ms Bernadette Leigh
Spotlight: Won for the second time over hurdles when scoring at Punchestown in May (form franked) over this trip; raised 7lb for that and is up in grade but goes well fresh so has to be respected.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won this last year off a 3lb lower mark; some good hurdle runs in defeat after while also won over fences; beaten 10l by Putapoundinthejar at Bellewstown last time but is 7lb better off so a player.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won three bumpers in France but is yet to score over hurdles for this yard; best run in a valuable handicap at Leopardstown in February but was poor in a maiden since; a player if back to best.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won a Limerick 4yo Grade 2 in 2022 but no win since; some decent efforts in defeat earlier this year but was well beaten in a 2m4f Punchestown handicap last time; the drop in trip may help.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Better known as a chaser and won a Ballinrobe handicap in that discipline in May; ran well on the first of two Flat starts since; hasn't run over hurdles since 2022 but could go well.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Exors of the Late E Blaney
Spotlight: Dual purpose winner won for the second time over hurdles when narrowly taking a 2m4f Killarney handicap last time; needs more down in trip off 7lb higher.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden in all spheres but was running a big race in a Cork maiden hurdle before falling last time; cheekpieces are added and capable of a decent showing.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual-purpose winner was below form over hurdles on his last two starts for Gavin Cromwell last winter; however, would have a chance off this mark if restored to his best.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Useful Flat sort on the continent has got his act together over hurdles, winning at Downpatrick and Killarney 109 days apart; seems best fresh but if he can back that up off 9lb higher then he is a player.

RaceName: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: D O'Mahony & D McHugh & D J Kelly & G Butler
Spotlight: Yet to win on the Flat but took a Down Royal maiden hurdle in May; might have been unsuited by soft ground when poor in a Roscommon novice last time; solid fourth on the Flat here on Thursday.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 450,000gns yearling; disappointing when sent off favourite for his Salisbury debut (7f, soft) in June, but with a tongue-tie fitted he showed his true colours when winning a Kempton novice (7f, AW) last month; has a 7lb penalty to carry, but bred to be smart so could easily step forward again.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Sent off 100-1 when beaten miles into last of 13 on his Southwell debut (7f, AW) nine days ago; stable runs three.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 50-1 when a well-beaten last of six on his Redcar debut (7f, good to firm) 13 days ago; hood worn then now removed.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Offered promise when fourth of ten in a Doncaster maiden (1m, soft) on his debut September, but well held on his Hamilton return (1m, good to firm) 16 days ago; looks one for handicaps.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Huge prices and failed to beat a rival in his first two starts (7f/1m2f) eight months apart; handicaps beckon.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has shown promise in both starts, even when last of three at Chester (1m2f, good) last month (runner-up has won since); shortlisted for stable that took this in 2022 and 2023.

RaceName: Theakston Great Yorkshire Pint EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in both starts, looking unlucky not to win having been badly hampered at Beverley (8.5f, good) last time; major player.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 380,000gns yearling; by Dark Angel; dam 5f/5.5f winner (including 2yo/Listed; RPR 99), half-sister to 5f-6f winner Marching Mac, out of 1m winning half-sister to 7f Group 3 winner Muthabara; expensive purchase with a useful pedigree and representing a leading local yard.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Stradivarius; dam placed 7f 2yo (RPR 70), half-sister to useful winners Not Never (1m1f 2yo/1m4f Flat and 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase) and Final Watch (7f); may be of more interest in the longer term.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Frankel; sister to 1m3f/2m2f Flat (RPR 84) and 2m/2m1f hurdle winner Secret Force, half-sister to 7f winner Cerro Blanco (103); dam 7f/1m winner (including 2yo/Listed; 107), out of Group-placed 7f 2yo winner; stable won this race in 2017, 2020 and 2024 and has a strike-rate of over 40% with its 2yos this season.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 200,000euros yearling; Coulsty half-sister to winners Pierre Bonnard (1m/1m2f 2yo including Group 1; RPR 119), Crepe Suzette (Group-placed 9.4f; 110) and Diavolo (7f; 91); dam 1m2f-1m4f winner (including Group 1 Nassau Stakes; 116); has a classy pedigree; stable's 2yos operating at 19% this season.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Quite stoutly bred and predictably improved for the step up to 7f when third here (good to firm; 33-1) two weeks ago; the type to progress with racing and should be involved in the shake-up once more.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Slowly away and always behind both starts; may benefit from today's step up in distance but needs a giant leap forward.

RaceName: Lodge At The National Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Kingman; sister to winners Calyx (6f including 2yo Group 2; RPR 118), Coppice (7f/1m including 2yo/Listed; 117) and Stanage (7f; 92); dam 6f-1m 2yo winner (including Group 3; 112), sister to 6f Group 1 winner African Rose; has an excellent Juddmonte pedigree and her stable's 2yos are just beginning to fire; big player on paper.

Duelled with Consent over 1m6f last year; progressive ways continued in May with a win at Newmarket (substandard 1m4f Group 2, good to firm) and close second in Group 1 at Longchamp (near 2m, soft); the Hardwicke back over 1m4f at Royal Ascot six weeks ago was a stiff task and she hung right in first-time cheekpieces on her way to a heavy defeat; much more interesting today with no headgear and back up in trip.

Pipped by Santorini Star in Group 2 at Doncaster (14.5f, good to soft) in September but turned the tables on her in fine style in Group 1 at Longchamp (1m6f, soft) in October; cut out tamely in the final 2f of another French Group 1 (near 2m, soft) on return but ten weeks have passed; never having raced on firmer than good asks quite a question but tough to beat if back to her best.

Second to Waardah in this last year and fourth to Santorini Star and Consent in Group 2 at Doncaster (14.5f, good to soft) last September; routed her rivals in Listed event (1m2f, heavy) in November and reappeared with Group 3 win at York (1m6f, good; made most at 1-2) ten weeks ago; unraced on good to firm since 2024 (comfortably held); serious player if the ground is okay.

5l third to Waardah in this last year, before career best when second in the Melbourne Cup (2m); back to best European form when second in Group 3 at Fairyhouse (1m6f, good; unraced on firmer) this month but will probably have to settle for a place here if others show their best.

Won twice here (soft/good to soft) last summer, latterly when leading over 2f out in this race and seeing off Danielle's challenge by three-quarters of a length; ran moderately on final 3yo start but reappearance this May was positive when second to a class act in Group 3 at Carlisle (1m3f, good to firm); big player if back to her peak.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Reappeared with 2l win in the Listed Cheshire Oaks at Chester (11.3f, good); soundly beaten when favourite for the Oaks itself on testing ground at Epsom and put firmly in her place when fifth in Irish Oaks at the Curragh (1m4f, good to firm; 5-1); wore a hood and blinkers on first two starts this season, just cheekpieces on latest; some limitations have seemingly been exposed and others saw the race out better in her two Oaks bids.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
OwnerName: G H Thompson And Michael Dods
Spotlight: No match for a subsequent winner at Redcar in May (6f, good) but that was a promising start; pressed the leader and kept on; can improve.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Low-level form thus far (over 5f) and likely to fare better when handicapping.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 8,000gns yearling; half-sister to 5f winner Beerwah (RPR 70); dam placed 5f-1m (102), sister to 7f winner Jalaad; stable's newcomers are usually best watched.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: The form of her second places give her a chance but now 0-7 and very disappointing in her last two races, latterly tried in cheekpieces.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 5,000gns yearling; 13th foal; half-sister to five winners including Staxton (6f; RPR 106), Lazarus Bell (7f 2yo; 89), Classic Pursuit (prolific 5f/6f; 89) and Satin Snake (7f; 81); dam 1m4f winner (80); rare 2yo runner for the yard.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 5,000gns foal; seventh foal; half-sister to 7f winner One Night Thunder (RPR 93); dam 6f AW winner (91), out of 1m4f/2m winning sister to Group 2 winners Nearly Caught (1m7f) and Pale Mimosa (2m); the market should be informative.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beaten 2l and less in her last three starts, all over 6f; narrowly denied last time at Chepstow (good to firm) and shouldn't be far away, unless there's a useful newcomer lurking.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 13,000gns yearling; sixth foal; half-sister to winners Ziggy's Triton (multiple 5f; RPR 96), Soller Bay (6f-1m1f; 68) and Mullazem (7f/1m); dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo winner Furas; stable had a newcomer win on debut earlier this week.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Eighth foal; half-sister to winners Militia (5f/6f; RPR 93), Faster Bee (7f; 76) and Shamadram (6f-1m); dam placed 1m AW 2yo (71), half-sister to winners Tactician (1m6f Listed) and Promotion (Listed-placed 1m2f); trainer having a good season with his 2yos.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 10,000euros 2yo; second foal; dam 1m-1m4f winner (RPR 87), closely related to winners Green Storm (Group-placed 1m1f 2yo) and Bulldog Spirit (1m-1m6f); trainer has sent out ten 2yo winners on turf this season.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to 6f/7f winner Eye Of Dubai (RPR 97); dam French 7.5f-1m2f winner, half-sister to German 1m3f winner Sokol; makes sense to check the betting.

RaceName: 7 Core Electrical Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For horses In Band D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 16,000gns yearling and half-sister to a 6f winner; 18-1 at Epsom (7f, good to firm) but beaten only 2l after starting slowly; should be wiser this time and have every chance.
Formerly smart chaser when trained by Gordon Elliott, winning in Grade 2 company and placed in Grade 1 bumpers; not a bad hurdle run last time at Worcester but this is much more competitive.
Won over fences last time at Wexford (2m3f); dual hurdle winner and has posted some smart form in this sphere over shorter; has a chance if getting back to best hurdle form and staying this trip.
Second runner for UK yard; won for the fifth time over hurdles at Uttoxeter last time, scoring by 11l over 2m4f; has to be respected even up 10lb and looks likely to stay too.
Six hurdle wins in Britain; some solid runs in defeat in quality handicaps since his last win including at Plumpton last time; needs more but shouldn't be far away either.
Last win came in a Listed hurdle in November at Kempton over 2m5f; some good runs after but was below form at Cheltenham; a decent Flat run last time at Tramore; considered.
Is 1-12 over hurdles; well beaten back on the Flat at Royal Ascot last time; needs a return to best hurdle form but can't be ruled out.
Came back to form in terrific style when winning the Connacht Hotel Flat Handicap over 2m on Monday here; hasn't run over hurdles since May 2025 but can be a big player with his confidence boosted.

Bumper and maiden hurdle winner looked set to score over 3m at Wexford before being run down by Kiltealy Park; similar effort in a Roscommon novice down to 2m since; needs more back in a handicap but considered.
Dual bumper winner is 2-8 over hurdles, both wins coming over about 2m; solid runs in defeat in 2m4f handicaps the last twice and should be competitive off same mark.
The last of his four hurdle wins came in this race in 2023 off 4lb higher; mostly chasing since and blinkers added; others more likely here.
Dual-purpose sort has been soundly beaten on his last three hurdle runs and needs a return to his best.

Won a valuable 2m handicap here in 2023 and won over fences after; solid runs at Wexford and Bellewstown lately, with the latter run looking better after the win of Putapoundinthejar in the Galway Hurdle; can run a sound race if staying.
Five wins between hurdles and fences up to 3m; decent runs in defeat over hurdles and fences last twice so one to consider.
Point and hurdle winner has been soundly beaten over fences lately but would have a shout on his best hurdles form of last year.
Promising sort last autumn, winning a maiden and second in a novice hurdle; however, he has to rebound in a major way from two pulled-up runs.
Has posted five wins between hurdles and fences; beat Dani Donadoni in a conditions race over 3m at Wexford last time; a 6lb rise makes this a tougher task but promising 5lb claimer helps.
Doubled his score over hurdles when winning well at Roscommon last time, beating Stede Bonnet; however, his record is still only 2-29 and a 7lb rise makes this a tougher task up in grade.
Won at Kilbeggan in June, his fifth hurdle win, but was beaten a long way there since so has to bounce back in a competitive race.
Bumper winner in 2023 built on his Clonmel maiden win when scoring at Limerick on handicap debut, both over approx' 2m4f; up 10lb but is an improving sort and should stay this trip.
Some decent runs in dxefeat in bumpers; won a Listowel maiden over 2m4f and was just denied in a Bellewstown handicap over 3m since; up 3lb but improving sort can be competitive.
Wasn't winning out of turn when taking a 5f handicap at Wolverhampton in May; didn't get the clearest run at Chester three weeks ago but that took his turf record to 0-11; others are more appealing.
Successful off this mark at Wolverhampton in March; solid efforts on his last three starts and he should make a bold bid to win this race for the second season in succession.

Won a 5f handicap off this mark at Newmarket (good to firm) last August; she has run some fair races this year but her latest effort (tried in cheekpieces, usual visor back on today) wasn't one of them; no surprise to see her bounce back quickly.
C&D winner; below par in a big field at York (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago but plenty of form this season that makes him of interest; Jack Callan's claim a bonus; one to consider back at 5f.
5f AW win in April; ran well at Ripon (5f, good) later that month but he has struggled twice since; has a C&D win on his record but others bring more pressing claims.

Prominent racer; thriving this season, winning three of his last five starts with the latest a cosy success at Hamilton (5f, good to firm) two weeks ago; up 4lb but he needs serious consideration; stable also runs American Bay.

OwnerName: Miss K Padgett And Mrs S D Pearson
Spotlight: Well handicapped on this winter's AW form but he has gone off the boil more recently; given a chance by the handicapper as a consequence and he needs a market check starting out for Ruth Carr (sold out of David Loughnane's stable for 22,000gns last month).
Didn't run badly at Windsor in May but that run is sandwiched by two lesser turf runs; connections now turn to a tongue tie and cheekpieces.
Talented veteran but has temperament to match his ability; no turf win since 2021 and when second at Nottingham 11 days ago there were only four runners; more minor money perhaps his best hope.
Two 5f wins this year and she ran her best race so far when third of 12 at York (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago; races off the same mark here and should make another bold bid.
Has a couple of C&D wins on his record; not found his best form this year and he has too much to prove for comfort, for all he is tumbling down the weights.
Three wins in 5f handicaps this year, the latest off 6lb lower last month; another good effort when second over 6f here last week; likely vulnerable in Class 4.

Campaigned over as far as 10.3f but proved well suited by the drop back to 7f when winning in clearcut style at Yarmouth (good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) last month; now that connections have found the key, she's open to further improvement; leading contender.
Thriving on this course this summer, and beat Lion Of Mali a neck over C&D three weeks ago; edging up the weights only slowly and should give another good account of himself.
Unlucky over this trip at Sandown two outings ago from just 1lb lower, but was disappointing when only fourth there next time; hasn't had much racing and may get back on the up.

Narrowly beaten on three of his four starts since being gelded, going down on the nod at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) on latest; should go close again off an unchanged mark, especially if first-time headgear has a positive effect.
Likeable 7f specialist (all four wins at this trip); just edged out by Sierra Sands over C&D three weeks ago; holding his form really well and should be in the thick of things again.
Sprang a 25-1 upset on debut at Newbury (6f) last summer, but unplaced all outings since, including over 1m4f last time; plummeting in the weights but hard to fancy.

He didn't make his debut until December but this 5yo is quickly making up for lost time, finishing third in a Listed race at Salisbury (6f, good) on his stable debut and then running a huge race in the Wokingham at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm), beaten just over one length into third off a 1lb lower mark; again raced freely when third in a Group 3 at Newbury (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago; still has potential after just six starts.

Would have finished closer than tenth in the Wokingham at Royal Ascot (6f) granted a clear run; scaled new heights when beating his 14 rivals there (5f, also good to firm) three weeks ago, finishing his race off strongly; 3lb wrong under his penalty today and while he has more good races in him, this one might prove too demanding.

Two wins in Dubai early in the year before coming up short in Group 1 company in March and June; back on the up with a 7f Listed win at Chester three weeks ago; this looks a tough task under 6lb penalty though.

He hasn't had a great deal of racing since July 2024 but, two wind surgeries and a gelding operation later, he has shown he retains a good chunk of his former ability (Group 2 winner at best) this year, in a tongue-tie on last two starts; finished just behind Soldier's Tree when fifth in the Wokingham (6f, good to firm) but was in front of that rival in a Group 3 at Newbury two weeks ago; 3lb well in and has the ability to feature but his tendency to forfeit ground at the start isn't ideal in a race of this depth.

Quickly established himself as a smart sprinter, winning Group 2 and Group 3 prizes at Meydan (both 5f; good to firm and good) in early 2025; the addition of cheekpieces saw him return to his best when second in a 5f Group 3 on Dundalk AW last October; not quite at his best in two runs in Dubai in January and absent since; new blinkers need to have a positive effect.

Climbed the ranks as a 4yo, ending that campaign with placed efforts in the Ayr Silver Cup and at Ascot; down the field on seasonal return but he hasn't looked back since, winning at Epsom (6f, soft) on Derby day for the second year in succession, doing best of the low numbers in the Wokingham (the others in his group have done well since) and then seeing off 19 rivals at the Curragh (6.3f, good to firm) two weeks ago; showed a fantastic attitude on that latest occasion and his 6lb penalty shouldn't prevent another big performance.

Finished fourth behind stablemate Two Tribes in this race 12 months ago when 8lb lower and enjoyed his finest hour when making most to win the Ayr Gold Cup (6f, soft) last September; successful in Dubai early in the year and although his results have been mixed since returning to Britain, he retains plenty of ability; down the field over 5f here on Tuesday when a change of tactics failed to bear fruit; better can be expected today.

Surged to the front 1f out when dominant in this race (good to soft) 12 months ago; 7lb higher this time around but he was better than ever when second in a hot handicap at Ascot last week (7f, good to firm) when coming from further back than ideal; 2lb ahead of the handicapper and he has a fine chance of becoming the fifth horse to win back-to-back Stewards' Cups (Commanche Falls in 2021 and 2022 was the latest).

Made all up the stands' rail when springing a 40-1 surprise in this race in 2024; added another major handicap when dominating last year's Wokingham; failed to beat a rival in his next three starts though (including in this race) and he has been absent for 314 days; his draw gives him the chance to repeat the heroics of 2024 but this looks a tough assignment on his return.

Finished eighth behind Two Tribes in this race 12 months ago when 4lb lower; he is a better horse now, as emphasised by two 6f AW wins in January and a fine second in the Wokingham (cheekpieces first time) but he finished behind Two Tribes at Ascot last week and others look more appealing for win purposes.

Won five of his ten starts for Richard Fahey, notably a local Group 3 in Qatar in November 2024; absent for 593 days and gelded prior to his stable debut at Pontefract (6f, good) last month, a race in which he was caught out wide but plugged on for second behind the thriving easy winner; clearly retains ability but this will demand much more.

Blessed with a potent turn of foot and he has been impressive in winning 6f AW handicaps at Kempton and Newcastle this year; a 3lb rise for the latter success five weeks ago doesn't handicap him out of things and he ran well in his one visit to Goodwood; one to be interested in.

Looked one to follow when bolting up at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in December; had numerous excuses for a series of subsequent defeats but things finally clicked again at York (6f, good to firm) last week, gamely repelling 20 rivals; 2lb wrong under his penalty but he has Group-race aspirations and shouldn't be passed over lightly.

Having edged down the weights he offered a good deal more when third to Tuco Salamanca at Newcastle (6f, AW) in June; finished with a flourish when seventh behind Dubai Bling at Ascot (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago, a run that confirmed he was still in good order; returning to 6f will help and he can't be dismissed, for all that he has been well beaten in this race twice before (2022 and 2025).

His impressive Newmarket success last May saw him hit hard by the handicapper and he hasn't added to it; chasing home Sondad at Epsom (6f, soft) in June represented his best run of the year but he failed to build on it at Windsor last time; others look safer.

6f winner at Thirsk (good) in May and back at a similar level when a keeping-on third behind Dubai Bling at Ascot (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago; should run his race but others are perhaps better treated.

Another success story for James Owen, progressing well in 2025 and continuing the good work this time around with wins over C&D and at Newbury (both good ground); another step forward when fourth in the Wokingham, an effort that can be upgraded, and he races off the same mark today; 3-3 over C&D and sure to be popular.

On the up in 2025, completing a hat-trick before fine runs at Royal Ascot and in the Ayr Gold Cup (beaten favourite in this race in between); had a wind operation prior to reappearance but he has finished down the field in both starts since, the Wokingham on latest; down in the weights but a full revival is essential; tongue-tie experiment last time is quickly aborted.

Profile is hit and miss but conditions won't faze him; he looked good at Carlisle (6f, good to firm; cheekpieces first time) in May and brings relatively low mileage but he was only midfield in the Wokingham and is 1lb higher today, so needs a big personal best.
Still has low mileage and is proven over C&D but he has come up well short in deep races since winning here last August; hood left off this time; others look safer.

OwnerName: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
Spotlight: He has done all his winning on AW but his fourth at Leicester (6f, good to firm) in April is a comparable standard; can win races on the grass but perhaps not this one.

Best known for his AW exploits but he is fine on turf and has a lower mark in this sphere; went desperately close at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) 15 days ago, a race in which the first two pulled clear in the closing stages from a subsequent winner; 2lb ahead of the handicapper and he was successful on his only visit to Goodwood; interesting.

Impressed at Windsor (6f, good to firm) in June; had an excuse at Ascot next time and spent the first half of the race in the unfavoured stands' side group when down the field there last week; this looks too demanding all the same.

Beat his 21 rivals at York in May and added a handicap at Chester (6f, good) last month; ran a fine race behind Sondad at the Curragh two weeks ago and is 7lb better off for half a length this time; officially the best handicapped horse in the race (5lb ahead of his mark) and another big run should be forthcoming.

Chased home Far Above Dream, beaten a neck with the pair clear, in a C&D handicap in May; again finished behind that rival in the Wokingham six weeks ago (cheekpieces first time) and needs more to win but that is not out of the question.

Three front-running AW wins in the spring saw him soar up the handicap; he didn't run badly off his revised mark at Epsom on Derby day but it would be a surprise if he were up to a task of this magnitude.

OwnerName: L Bond & Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi
Spotlight: Has a history of running well at this meeting and Tuesday's fourth (5f, good) was another solid effort; this looks a much stiffer test though.
All the better for a hood returning, winning two of his last three races; overcame some traffic issues to prevail narrowly at Windsor 12 days ago (1m2f, good to firm); 3lb higher.
Won at Ripon (1m, soft) last July off a mark 12lb higher than today's but he's struggled since; others have stronger claims.
Some return to form in his last two races and wasn't far away over 1m here last time when a stronger pace would have helped; interesting returned to further, having won over this far.
Won twice over 9.4f on the AW during the winter; probably okay on turf (0-4) but last two runs were heavy defeats and she's been off since March.

Only 1-27, the win when with Ralph Beckett; had been badly out of form this season but ran better in a new tongue-tie over 1m here last time when close up behind Mariner; possibilities if as good again as he stays this far.
Has shown some fair Flat form but became disappointing for David O'Meara and has shown nothing over hurdles for current yard.
Well handicapped on his form up to June 2023 but he was then absent until this season and hasn't been the force of old on his three runs in 2026.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Impressive on 2yo debut in 2024 (6f, good) then absent until last month, when going very close at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) before easy win at 1-50 at Lingfield (6f, good to firm); could be on a good mark for this first handicap.

Well beaten on final outing last season and same story on reappearance at Epsom on Oaks day (pulled hard); he has something to prove but that latest outing may have got the freshness out of him and he's on a handy mark on last season's best efforts; not written off.
Won at Lingfield (1m, AW) in April and achieved his best result of this turf season when close fourth of 17 at York (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago; he might not be far away.

Very lightly raced since winning two 2yo novice races in autumn 2024 (7f, AW); returned from another absence at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in April, having been gelded, and ran well in second of six; could have part to play.

Reappeared at York (7f, good) in June following a wind op and he beat 19 rivals to win; very much of interest based on that performance but he was well beaten back at York (7f, good to firm) last time; cheekpieces go on.

Won over C&D (good) in May and close second at Chester (7f, good) a fortnight later; respectable sixth of 19 at York (7f, good) next time and perhaps unsuited by return to AW most recently; each-way possibilities.

Won four times in 2024; just two runs last year and reappeared this April with close third at Redcar; down to a dangerous mark but he hasn't really shone on his last four starts and has to turn things around.

8yo who was knocking on the door prior to making all in fine style at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) 12 days ago; had just three rivals to beat last time and he's 4lb higher in a tougher race today, but is clearly in good heart and is a two-time winner at Thirsk; could go well.

Ran really well when runner-up in two big-field handicaps at York (7f/1m, good) in June; not at the same level when mid-division there (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago in first-time cheekpieces (retained) but can be in the shake-up if swiftly rediscovering his previous form.

OwnerName: Ursa Major Racing Ltd & Julie Camacho
Spotlight: Won in fields of a similar size to today's at York (7f, good) last July and Wetherby (7f, good to firm) in June; outside of those wins his form figures since last June read 000089055 and he's a type who needs everything to drop right, but it's possible that will happen off an expected good pace today.
Won at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) in May and has run well in defeat at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) and Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) on his last two starts; he's in with an each-way chance.

Four-time AW winner, the latest at Newcastle (7f) in May, and good second at Chester (7f, good to soft) in June; however, only fifth of ten at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last time and has to leave that run behind if he's to get off the mark on turf at the seventh attempt.

Without a win since August 2024 but he's been in good form since this visor went on, bumping into an unexposed 3yo when second of four at Catterick (7f, good to firm) and again finishing runner-up at Chester (7.5f, good) last time; in each-way calculations once more.
She's dropped below her last winning mark and has run some reasonable races on turf this summer, but without suggesting a win is imminent; she's just 1-20 on grass as opposed to 6-43 on AW.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Has run to a similar level in all three starts; beaten 8.5l when seventh of 16 at Roscommon latest (2m, good); should be sharper for that but needs more to get her head in front.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Point-to-point winner finished 2.75l behind Aodha's Arrow on Rules' debut in a Roscommon bumper when 11-1; major improvement required.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Best effort yet when finishing ahead of Aodha's Arrow and Back In Favour at Roscommon on latest; should strip fitter for that run and holds an each way chance.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: 40-1 but creditable effort on debut at Killarney last month, showing up well before fading in the final furlong into a 6.5l third of 15; likely to improve for that run and outside place claims.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Poet's Word mare; dam bumper/2m hurdle winner, sister to smart bumper and 2m2f-2m6f hurdle winner Glens Melody, closely related to useful 2m-3m hurdle winner Lean Araig, out of 2m Flat, bumper and useful 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase winner; lots of appeal on paper and top yard has won five of last six renewals.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Belied odds of 66-1 to run a huge race on debut at Roscommon when she had a few of these behind; enters calculations now with improvement likely to be forthcoming.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Heavy defeats at big odds in bumpers at Roscommon and Wexford; seems safe to rule out.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Modest enough efforts in bumpers at Leopardstown when beaten 16l into fourth and at Limerick when beaten 32l into fifth; new cheekpieces need to eke out more.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
OwnerName: Whose Round Is It Now Syndicate
Spotlight: Wide margin point-to-point winner on soft in April at Tullaherin; promising start under Rules when a 2.75l third of 14 at Wexford in May and the second from that race has won a bumper easily since; big player on that form.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Promise in all three starts; beaten similar distances when fifth on debut at Cork and again on second start at Wexford; didn't get a clear run when beaten 3.5l into fourth at Sligo on latest; can give another good account.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Displayed potential on debut at Limerick (2m, soft) two months ago, outpaced but keeping on for a 9.75l third of 9; should come on for that and now sports a tongue tie; not discounted for place purposes.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Okay effort when fourth at Tramore on debut; didn't build on that when tailed off at Cork latest; others preferred.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: One of two for top yard that has won five of last six renewals; Doctor Dino filly; half-sister to winners Fleur In The Park (smart bumper and 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase), Zurekin (useful 2m1f/2m2f hurdle), Hunting Brook (2m5f/3m hurdle) and Marie Philippe (bumper); dam useful 2m1f-2m5f chase winner; preferred by Patrick Mullins.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt in point-to-points at Loughrea in May; bought for E35,000 at Tattersalls later that month; probably best watched on Rules' debut; tongue tied.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: 25-1 and beaten 25l on debut at Tramore in May; others make more appeal.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Harzand filly; half-sister to winners Phantom Gold (bumper/2m4f hurdle) and Parisian Fashion (2m4f hurdle); dam useful bumper and 2m/2m1f hurdle winner; makes some appeal on paper and worth checking in the market; tongue tied.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
OwnerName: For The Love Of It Syndicate
Spotlight: Off the mark at the second attempt in point-to-points at Lisronagh for Benny Walsh in April; has joined a shrewd yard that has already had a winner here this week and this daughter of Yeats needs checking in the market on Rules' debut; tongue tied.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Placed in one of two starts in point-to-points; bought for E25,000 after finishing second of four finishers at Oldcastle; percentage call is to watch on Rules' bow.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
OwnerName: Going For The One Syndicate/Michael McEvoy/Jimmy Whittle
Spotlight: Was bang there when falling at the last in sole point-to-point start at Lisronagh in April; bumper winners in pedigree and yard had a bumper winner at Ballinrobe last month; market can guide on Rules' debut.

RaceName: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Old Persian filly; half-sister to winners Miami Present (useful 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase) and Florida Calling (point); dam German 7f/7.5f winner, half-sister to 1m Listed Flat and useful 2m-2m2f hurdle/chase winner Moon Over Miami; market can guide on debut.

Ten-time AW winner who is 5lb lower than when winning at Southwell (1m4f, AW) last November; however, this is his first run since January and he was well beaten at Ascot in May 2024 on his last encounter with turf; 0-5 on grass and others have less to prove.

He's had a long career but never been better than this season, winning on AW at Wolverhampton (9.4f) and Lingfield (1m4f); they were in March/April but he returned from a break with creditable third of six here (1m2f, good to firm) 15 days ago, again under Olivia Tubb; probably not far away.

Has done well over 1m4f-1m6f on turf this term, winning three times from six starts; latest win came easily at this track (1m6f, good to firm) in June and he's 7lb higher today; tailing off so badly at Southwell four weeks ago may be offputting but he came last in 2025 in his only other AW race, so perhaps can spring back to life with today's return to turf.
Gained his most recent win here (1m6f) last August off 2lb lower in first-time blinkers; with creditable shows in two of his three starts this season, he is firmly in calculations.

OwnerName: S Mizon, H McAlpine & Winner Racing Ltd
Spotlight: Has some back-class but now 0-11 for this yard and the form he showed in initial outings last summer has not been repeated; accelerating down the weights, which gives him a chance on this year's form even, but others are more convincing.

5yo now who won for Sean Woods on belated debut last July; no joy in his seven races since, three for this yard, but he kept on well for a good third of 12 in a slowly run race at Ayr (upped markedly to 1m5f, soft) in June and may well have been stretched by 1m6f when performing respectably at Ascot (good to firm; made most) three weeks ago; firmly in the mix.

Both wins (from nine races) have been in small fields, including from off the pace at Lingfield (1m2f, good to firm) on reappearance ten days ago; going back up 4lb demands more but there's a fair chance that he'll turn out to be an improved performer this term; up 2f, which he's not sure to stay, but he has to be on the shortlist.

Often ridden by claimer Alexandra Egan, including when he won a four-runner C&D race (good to firm) last July off the same mark as today; creditable second on last two outings (C&D latest) suggest he will be bang there.

Spotlight: The class angle in this field and has earned top weight on handicap debut, having ended his progressive 2yo season with good efforts in a Newmarket Group 2 (7f, good to firm) and Canadian Grade 1 (1m, firm); a likely danger provided he's back in similar form with Listed reappearance under his belt.
Commenced career with a record of 221 on AW; far from solid on his Listed/Group form on turf since (peak effort may not be reliable) and has something to prove off his mark; gelded since last run.

Gelded since finishing last when favourite for the Britannia at Royal Ascot (1m); had progressive 7f form previously and recorded a wide-margin success at Newmarket (good) the time before, taking record over this trip to 2211; may still have more to offer and remains of interest.

Back in his comfort zone at Epsom (7f, good) last time, taking Class 4 record to 3-3; sold out of George Boughey's yard for 28,000gns since; returns to deeper waters off a demanding mark; new headgear.

Campaigned over shorter this term, posting a useful AW win on reappearance and not disgraced at Newmarket most recently; showed respectable 7f form as a 2yo, including a good effort in the maiden on this card and a success at Chester; still fairly unexposed over this distance; interesting.

Won on the nod at Doncaster (good to firm) last time, looking suited by the step up to 7f and surging back to form; unexposed over this trip and may remain competitive, provided he takes to first-time cheekpieces (faced difficult task when once in blinkers).

Took a while to hit the target but he had some notable maiden form, including at this meeting last year, and now bids for a hat-trick after wins under Jack Nicholls at Pontefract (6f maiden, good to soft) and Catterick (7f handicap; good to firm); further improvement is possible; respected.

Versatile sort who held on narrowly from Proud Nation over 7f at Newmarket (good to firm) most recently, adding to his 2yo sprint wins and taking record to 3-7; ran creditably over C&D in May; solid chance.

Low-mileage colt who registered his 2yo success in a York maiden and posted two sound efforts since handicapping, beaten narrowly by Ironwill at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) latest; may do better still; not ruled out.

Broadly progressive gelding who has form figures of 11127 in turf handicaps, the latest effort best forgiven (met trouble); ran well in a competitive field over C&D the time before; still 9lb above last winning mark but Harry Vigors takes off a useful 5lb; in the mix.

Prevailed narrowly in small field when upped to 7f at Newmarket (good to firm) last time, taking record to 2-4; goes into deeper waters but remains unexposed, particularly at this distance; wears first-time headgear.

Has form figures of 114, all at Chester (6f and around 7f), since being gelded (maiden previously); not disgraced last time but has something to prove off the same mark switched to a different venue and upped in grade.

Appears to have his limitations, being 2-2 in Class 5 but 0-5 in higher grades; gained the latest success at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) last week; opposed from 6lb out of the weights in this markedly better race.

Twice runner-up before winning a 7f AW maiden in October and then gelded; finished last of the four when favourite for his handicap debut at Catterick (7f, good to firm) but he raced freely up front and didn't look at home on the track; worth another chance.
Bought for 50,000gns soon after winning a 6f Curragh maiden in first-time cheekpieces (eighth start); proven over 1m, let alone this far, and could be interesting on yard/handicap debut.

Newmarket maiden winner for Harry Charlton last August (6f, good to firm); subsequently sold for 90,000gns; building momentum in handicaps for his new yard, last time holding every chance over C&D and going down by a length; solid prospects off 1lb lower.

OwnerName: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
Spotlight: 7f maiden winner in May and held his own in handicaps until a poor last run, since when he's been gelded; entitled to play a part if back to best.

Goodwood novice winner in May of last year; 0-9 in the meantime and progress has levelled out; ran no more than okay when third of five in a new tongue-tie last week at Lingfield (6f, good to firm); swaps cheekpieces for first-time blinkers here.

OwnerName: L Bond, Sheikh Aymen Al Hamandi, J Catling
Spotlight: 0-7 in Ireland with one notable effort when narrowly beaten in a 5f handicap at Naas in March (first-time blinkers); struggled in two following runs, the latest tried in a visor; changed hands for 5,500gns; likely best watched.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Exposed 6yo who concedes weight to 3yo rivals but brings positives, being the only C&D scorer in the field and a winner off 2lb higher in most recent attempt in this grade.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Novice win last October; has come up well short in Class 4 handicaps this term (modest fourth last time; gelded since) but may fare better off a reduced mark at this lower level.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Improved form the last twice, finishing first past the post at Goodwood (1m4f; demoted to second for causing interference) then beaten only a neck at Newbury (1m5f); respected.

RaceName: Vision PVC Carlton Miniott Thirsk Handicap
Spotlight: Five-race maiden who has two standout pieces of form, including creditable effort with cheekpieces fitted at Doncaster (1m4f) last time; could go well in the retained headgear.

Fifth foal; half-brother to winners Pinot Gris (10.3f/1m5f Flat, RPR 87; useful 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase) and Postdamerstrasse (Italian 7.5f); dam 1m4f/12.5f winner (85); E18,000 foal made E40,000 as a yearling; by a promising first-crop sire and related to winners so could run respectably.

First foal; dam twice-raced half-sister to winners Alluringly (9.4f Listed) and Toogood Tobetrue (useful 6f 2yo), from the family of Derby winners and oustanding sires Galileo and Sea The Stars; E300,000 yearling is the stable second-string on debut but is still respected.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Brother to 6f Group 2 2yo winner Beautify; was the stable second-string on debut when runner-up in what is traditionally a strong Curragh maiden; that was 7f but looked as if he would stay this trip; looks the one to beat on that run.

A 75,000gns breeze-up purchase in April and from a middle-distance family; recovered from a slow start to run well on debut at Killarney over this trip; can be more competitive with that experience behind him.

OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Has taken a while to get the hang of things, but improved form last two starts, winning novice in small field at Nottingham and pulling clear with the winner when second in handicap at Salisbury (both 1m2f, good to firm); tactically versatile and looks the one to beat.
6f winner last autumn; has been running respectably in 7f/1m handicaps without looking ahead of her mark; now moves up in distance (sister won up to 1m2f); should be thereabouts.

280,000gns purchase as a yearling; hasn't gone on as anticipated from a promising debut, fading and beating only one home in maiden at Yarmouth (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago; still early days but she has something to prove.
Two wins from ten outings, both over the extended 1m at Nottingham; faded on first attempt at 1m2f when fifth at Windsor last time; beginning to look exposed.
